The figure shows the average OoV rate across all users for different vocabulary sizes, evaluated on a range of test sets collected every Tuesday between 2011/10/11-2012/01/03. The lines represent the OoV rates for different dates, with each line corresponding to a specific date. The y-axis represents the OoV rate, and the x-axis represents the vocabulary size. The figure is plotted on a log-scale, which means that the y-axis values are logarithmic. This suggests that the OoV Rate is calculated based on the ratio of out-of-vocabulary words to the total number of words in the text, and the log-scale indicates that the OoV Rate decreases as the vocabulary size increases. The effect of the OoV Rate on the results is that a higher OoV Rate can lead to a decrease in the performance of language models, as they may not be able to handle the out-of-vocabulary words correctly.
